### Position read
Opening position. We moved Red from (0,3) to (3,3), taking the upper-left center square. Losses are all 0; no colors are eliminated.

### Our plan
Contest the center aggressively with both colors while watching for same-color sandwich geometry. Yellow can approach (4,3) or (4,4), depending on the opponent’s reply. Preserve clear rook lanes and avoid clustering teammate pieces between same-colored opposing flanks.

### Opponent tendencies
No moves observed yet.

### Lessons
Captures trigger only from the landing piece and require its own color as both sandwich ends; teammate pieces can be friendly-fire victims. Moving into a sandwich is safe.

### Position read
We occupy center squares (3,3) with Red and (4,3) with Yellow. The opponent occupies (4,4) with Blue; (3,4) is empty. Losses remain 0 and no color is eliminated.

### Our plan
Maintain our adjacent central pair. Yellow on (4,3) threatens a future move to (4,5), which would sandwich Blue on (4,4) if it stays. If Blue retreats, seek occupation of (4,4); continue using Red to contest (3,4). Check every central move for enclosure and friendly-fire effects.

### Opponent tendencies
Blue immediately contested the center by moving from (4,7) to (4,4).

### Lessons
Adjacent same-team colors do not form capture flanks, but they do count together for center victory. A positioned same-color piece can turn a later landing move into a sandwich.

### Position read
We now occupy (3,3) and (3,4) with Red and (4,3) with Yellow; Blue occupies the final center square (4,4). Green has advanced to (5,5). All losses are still 0.

### Our plan
We have a three-square center lock, so pressure Blue on (4,4). If it vacates without blocking the vertical route, Yellow from (7,4) can fill (4,4) for an immediate center win while Yellow remains on (4,3). If Blue retreats to (5,4) to block that route, preserve the central trio and develop a Yellow route toward (4,5) or another way to dislodge it. Avoid vacating any occupied center unnecessarily.

### Opponent tendencies
Blue contested (4,4) immediately; Green moved across to (5,5), potentially obstructing Yellow's route from (7,5) toward (4,5).

### Lessons
A center defender may retreat onto a reinforcement line, so verify that the intended replacement can actually reach the vacated square. Rook paths cannot cross the piece being targeted.

### Position read
We hold center squares (3,3) and (4,3); the opponent holds (4,4), while (3,4) is empty. We have lost one Red piece; all other loss counts are 0. Yellow is now at (5,4), below the opponent’s central piece, with Green at (5,5).

### Our plan
Use Yellow (5,4) as a flank. If Green remains on (5,5) and (5,6) stays open, Yellow from (7,6) can land on (5,6) and capture it. If Green relocates to (4,5), Yellow from (7,6) may later land on (4,6), sandwiching the entire line through (4,5) and (4,4) against our Yellow at (4,3). Preserve our two occupied center squares and seek control of (3,4).

### Opponent tendencies
The opponent uses Blue pairs tactically: the move to (2,4) captured our piece at (3,4) against Blue at (4,4). Green has been used to obstruct reinforcement lanes.

### Lessons
Moving into an existing sandwich is safe, so positional flanks only capture when one endpoint later lands. Track blockers on (5,6) and (4,6), which can neutralize the planned Yellow landing captures.

### Position read
We hold (3,3) with Red and (4,3) with Yellow; the opponent holds (4,4). Our Yellow at (5,4) flanks Green at (5,5), and Red has now moved to (2,5), flanking Blue at (2,4). Only our Red has one recorded loss.

### Our plan
Two captures are threatened. Yellow can move (7,6)->(5,6) to sandwich Green at (5,5) against Yellow (5,4). If Blue at (2,4) remains, Red (3,3)->(2,3) can later sandwich it against Red (2,5). Prefer the immediate Yellow capture if (5,6) remains open. If Blue blocks (5,6), preserve the Red threat, while watching for Green occupying (2,3) before Red acts.

### Opponent tendencies
The opponent uses Blue to create central sandwich tactics and Green to obstruct landing squares. Expect Blue to save its piece at (2,4) or block (5,6), with Green potentially covering the other threat.

### Lessons
Coordinate threats across consecutive team turns, but account for the opponent’s intervening Green turn: Green can occupy (2,3) and prevent the planned Red landing.

### Position read
We hold central squares (3,3) with Red and (4,3) with Yellow; the opponent holds (4,4). Yellow has just moved to (5,6), sandwiching and capturing Green at (5,5) against Yellow (5,4). Losses should now be: our Red 1, opponent Green 1. Blue escaped the earlier Red sandwich by moving from (2,4) to (2,3).

### Our plan
Protect our two central occupants and seek control of (3,4) and (4,4) for center victory. On Red’s next turn, examine moves that pressure Blue (2,3) or dislodge/block the opponent’s central formation. Keep Yellow (5,4) and (5,6) coordinated for further horizontal tactics, while avoiding friendly-fire lines through our center.

### Opponent tendencies
The opponent recognized and escaped the threatened Blue sandwich. Expect Green to counterattack the newly advanced Yellow pair or occupy a key central/landing square.

### Lessons
Cash in a forced capture before the intervening color can obstruct it. Recalculate sandwich geometry after every escape; the former Red capture setup no longer works once Blue shifts to (2,3).

### Position read
We hold (3,3) and (4,3); the opponent holds (4,4). Red has moved to (2,4), blocking Green’s column-4 route into (3,4). Blue at (2,3) is now between Red (2,4) and a potential Red landing at (2,2). Yellow still threatens the center Blue via (7,5)->(4,5).

### Our plan
Exploit the fork. If the opponent saves Blue (2,3) and leaves (4,4), capture the center piece with Yellow; Red (2,4) can then enter (3,4), preserving Red (3,3), and Yellow can aim for (4,4) to complete center occupation. If Blue (4,4) moves to (3,4), pursue the exposed Blue at (2,3). Watch for Green blocking Red’s route from (0,2) to (2,2); if Green occupies (2,2), Red (0,1)->(2,1) may capture the whole line through Green and Blue.

### Opponent tendencies
The opponent prioritizes escaping visible sandwiches and contesting central squares. Expect Blue to use (3,4) as the main defensive square and Green to obstruct the follow-up capture.

### Lessons
Treat teammate pieces as neither sandwich partners nor enclosure walls. Preserve Red (3,3): together with Red (2,4), it supports a fast center win once Blue vacates (4,4).

### Position read
We occupy three center squares: Red (3,3), Yellow (4,3), Yellow (4,4); Blue alone blocks the fourth at (3,4). Red (2,4) and Blue (2,3) form a sandwich opportunity if Red can land at (2,2). Losses: we have Red 1, Yellow 0; opponent Blue 0, Green 1.

### Our plan
On Red’s next turn, capture Blue (2,3) with a landing at (2,2) if open. If Green blocks (2,2), inspect Red (0,1)->(2,1), which can capture a mixed line through the blocking Green and Blue to Red (2,4). Maintain our three central occupants. If Blue leaves (3,4), aim to place Red (2,4) there while Yellow holds (4,4), completing center occupation instantly.

### Opponent tendencies
The opponent prioritizes visible sandwich escapes and central defense. Green is likely to obstruct Red’s landing square or create a new blocker; Blue should remain at (3,4) unless forced.

### Lessons
Center occupation is checked immediately. Teammates do not form sandwich pairs, but mixed-color lines between two pieces of the moving color are captured together.

### Position read
Red moved (0,2)->(2,2), sandwiching and capturing Blue at (2,3). We retain three center squares: Red (3,3), Yellow (4,3), Yellow (4,4); opponent Blue at (3,4) is the sole center blocker. Losses should now be Red 1, Yellow 0; Blue 1, Green 1.

### Our plan
Keep all three central occupants. If Blue simply vacates (3,4) without capturing one, Yellow can move (4,4)->(3,4) on our immediately following turn for instant center victory. Otherwise assess captures against the new defense and preserve the center bind. Red (2,4) remains positioned to enter (3,4) later if it becomes empty before a Red turn.

### Opponent tendencies
The opponent prioritizes visible sandwich escapes and central defense. Blue is effectively pinned at (3,4) unless it can vacate while also removing a central piece; Green may try to disrupt our center before Red acts again.

### Lessons
Convert forced sandwich gains while maintaining center pressure. Center occupation wins immediately, and the moving color alone supplies both sandwich flanks.

### Position read
We hold three center squares: Red (3,3), Yellow (4,3) and (4,4); Blue (3,4) is the only blocker. Yellow moved (7,5)->(7,4), preserving the center and setting a sandwich against Blue (6,4). Losses: Red 1, Yellow 0; Blue 1, Green 1.

### Our plan
If the center remains intact, Red should stage (0,6)->(3,6). Then Blue at (3,4) must either stay and face Red (3,6)->(3,5), sandwiching it against Red (3,3), or vacate so Yellow can occupy (3,4) for an immediate center win. Independently, Yellow can play (5,6)->(5,4) to capture Blue (6,4) against Yellow (7,4), provided the line remains.

### Opponent tendencies
The opponent prioritizes central defense and escape from visible sandwiches. Expect Green to disrupt a central occupant or interfere with Red’s staging square if possible; expect Blue to answer direct center threats.

### Lessons
Preserve all three central occupants while building same-color flanks. A forced center vacancy is as valuable as a capture because occupation wins immediately.

### Position read
We occupy three center squares: Red (3,3), Yellow (4,3) and (4,4); Blue (3,4) is the blocker. Red is now staged at (3,6). Green moved to (4,5), beside our central Yellow. Losses: Red 1, Yellow 0; Blue 1, Green 1.

### Our plan
Red threatens (3,6)->(3,5), sandwiching Blue (3,4) against Red (3,3). If Blue vacates (3,4) without disrupting another center square, Yellow should fill (3,4) immediately for the center win. Watch Blue (6,4)->(5,4), which could sandwich Yellow (4,4) against Blue (3,4); if used, rebuild the center or seek captures with Yellow.

### Opponent tendencies
The opponent prioritizes central defense and uses off-center pieces to disrupt our established occupants. Green at (4,5) may reposition to interfere with Yellow’s center structure.

### Lessons
Direct center forks force defensive moves, but inspect remote same-color flanks before assuming the threat wins immediately. Preserve the three center occupants whenever possible.

### Position read
We hold Red at (3,3), Yellow at (4,3), and have staged Yellow at (4,6). Opponent Blue occupies (3,4) and (5,4); Green occupies (4,5). Losses: our Red 1, Yellow 1; opponent Blue 1, Green 1.

### Our plan
The opponent faces a center fork. If Green stays on (4,5), Red can play (3,6)->(3,5), sandwiching Blue (3,4) against Red (3,3). If Green moves (4,5)->(3,5) to block, Yellow’s path from (4,6) toward (4,4) opens. If Blue then occupies (4,4), Yellow can play (4,6)->(4,5), sandwiching that Blue against Yellow (4,3). Preserve our two current center occupants while forcing the opponent’s Blue toward a second loss.

### Opponent tendencies
The opponent prioritizes central defense and uses nearby pieces for immediate sandwich disruption. Expect Green to block Red or Blue to shift onto (4,4).

### Lessons
Coordinate threats across consecutive team turns. Empty transit squares can turn a defensive block by one opponent color into a sandwich opportunity against the other.

### Position read
We hold Red (3,3) and Yellow (4,3); opponent Blue holds (3,4). Green’s move from (4,5) to (3,5) opened Yellow’s route from (4,6) toward the center. Red remains at (3,6), so Blue (3,4) and Green (3,5) sit between two Red pieces, but the static sandwich does not capture. Losses remain one for every color.

### Our plan
Preserve our center pair and use Yellow next. If Blue moves onto (4,4), play Yellow (4,6)->(4,5) to sandwich it against Yellow (4,3). If Blue leaves (3,4) without occupying (4,4), strongly consider Yellow (4,6)->(4,4), taking a third center square. Keep Red (3,3) and (3,6) in place unless a concrete capture or center win requires moving them.

### Opponent tendencies
The opponent prioritizes blocking center occupation and used Green (3,5) to stop Red’s immediate horizontal capture. Expect Blue to contest (4,4) or reposition so Green can inherit (3,4).

### Lessons
Static flanks do not capture; preserve them for a future retrigger. When one defender blocks a capture lane, exploit the square it vacated to advance the other controlled color.

### Position read
We occupy three center squares: our Red at (3,3) and Yellow at (4,3),(4,4); the opponent holds (3,4). Our Red has two losses, so its next capture would eliminate it. Our Yellow pair at (4,4) and (7,4) also brackets the opponent Blue at (5,4) with (6,4) open as a future landing square.

### Our plan
Protect the three-square center formation and seek control of (3,4). On our next Yellow turn, if (5,4) remains occupied and (6,4) is clear, consider (7,4)->(6,4) to capture it against Yellow (4,4). Red should avoid exposure while looking for a move that retriggers the horizontal line around (3,4)-(3,5).

### Opponent tendencies
The opponent is actively disrupting our center and just captured a second Red piece. Expect Green to contest our center structure or Blue to vacate (5,4) before the Yellow sandwich.

### Lessons
A center advance can create a secondary sandwich threat. Treat our two-loss Red as tactically fragile and preserve its useful central anchor.

### Position read
Our Red is eliminated; its remaining Void pieces at (1,1),(2,3),(3,6) still move and count for center occupation but cannot capture. We hold Yellow at center squares (4,3),(4,4); both upper center squares are empty. Blue has two losses and a piece at (5,4), currently bracketable by Yellow (4,4) and (7,4) via landing at (6,4).

### Our plan
If (3,3) stays open, move the Void Red from (2,3) there next Red turn, advancing center occupation. On Yellow’s turn, if Blue remains at (5,4) and (6,4) is clear, play (7,4)->(6,4) to capture and eliminate Blue. Otherwise preserve the Yellow center pair and seek (3,4).

### Opponent tendencies
The opponent disrupted the center with a Green sandwich, eliminating Red while also capturing its own Blue. Expect Blue to flee (5,4) and Green to contest (3,3) or attack the Yellow center pair.

### Lessons
Void pieces cannot capture but remain valuable center occupants. Blue’s two-loss status makes the column-4 Yellow sandwich an elimination threat.

### Position read
Our Red is eliminated, so losing one more Yellow piece would eliminate our whole team immediately. Yellow now occupies (4,4). Blue has two losses and pieces at (3,4) and (5,4), surrounding Yellow harmlessly because moving into a sandwich is safe. Our Void Red at (2,3) can still help occupy the center.

### Our plan
On the next Red turn, if (3,3) remains open, move Void Red (2,3)->(3,3), giving us two center squares. Yellow threatens (7,4)->(6,4) to sandwich Blue at (5,4) against Yellow (4,4), so exploit it if Blue stays. Preserve every Yellow piece because any Yellow capture ends the game against us.

### Opponent tendencies
The opponent uses mixed-color sandwich lines effectively and will likely contest (3,3), move Blue from (5,4), or try to dislodge Yellow from (4,4).

### Lessons
Self-moving into an existing sandwich is safe. Void Red cannot capture but remains useful for center occupation and as a stationary Red wall.

### Position read
Our Red is eliminated and Yellow has two losses, so any Yellow capture immediately loses the game. We hold center (4,4); the opponent holds (3,3) and (3,4). Blue at (5,4) has two losses and is threatened by Yellow (7,4)->(6,4), sandwiching it against Yellow (4,4). Void Red moved to (4,1), blocking Green at (4,0) from sliding toward the center along row 4.

### Our plan
If Blue remains at (5,4), play Yellow (7,4)->(6,4) to eliminate Blue. If it retreats, strongly consider Yellow (4,4)->(4,3) to deny Green that center square, but first check all sandwich and enclosure consequences. Use Void Red from (4,1) toward (4,3) when the path opens; it cannot capture but counts for center occupation.

### Opponent tendencies
The opponent actively contests central squares and should retreat Blue from (5,4), then may use Green at (3,3) to occupy (4,3) or maneuver around our blocker.

### Lessons
Protect Yellow absolutely. Void pieces cannot capture, but they can block movement, occupy center squares, and safely move into sandwich formations.

### Position read
We have moved our normal piece from center (4,4) to center (4,3). Our first color is eliminated; our surviving color has two losses, so any capture of it ends the game. The opponent occupies centers (3,3) and (3,4), while (4,4) is empty. An opponent piece at (5,3) could sandwich our piece on (4,3) only if another opponent piece lands at (3,3), currently occupied by the opponent's other color.

### Our plan
If the opponent vacates (3,3), move our Void piece from (2,3) into (3,3), preventing the sandwich and securing another center. Otherwise make a safe Void move that preserves this blockade. Seek a one-piece capture against either opponent color, since each has two losses.

### Opponent tendencies
The opponent retreats threatened pieces and coordinates central occupation. Expect an attempt to clear (3,3) for a sandwich using the piece at (5,3), or to occupy the newly empty (4,4).

### Lessons
Our surviving color must never be exposed to capture. Before every move, check whether vacating or occupying a square enables a same-color sandwich on the opponent's following turn.
